summary: Intermittent duplicate function/tool invocations when uploading binary attachments through CDN edge during SDK retries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightWrite Labs reports intermittent duplicated downstream function/tool invocations when sending binary attachments (multipart/form-data) through their app that uses the Python SDK via our regional CDN/edge proxy. Duplicates only appear after the client issues retries (exponential backoff) following slow upstream responses or transient 504s.

Impact:
- Duplicate webhook/tool calls resulting in duplicated downstream side effects (some customers reported doubled billing records in their downstream system).
- Affects production traffic for BrightWrite Labs' dedicated tenant in us-west. Estimated ~0.7% of attachment upload requests in a 24h window (per customer telemetry) resulted in duplication.

Environment details:
- SDK: python-sdk 2.1.3 (customer)
- App uses multipart/form-data uploads with a binary blob (~1–4 MB) and metadata fields.
- Traffic routed through our edge CDN/HTTP2 terminator, then to api-gateway -> auth -> serving-runtime.
- Occurs in prod us-west only. Staging reproductions attempted in staging-edge.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Client sends a multipart/form-data request with fields: metadata JSON, file blob, and X-Client-Metadata headers.
2) Request stalls at edge for ~3–6s (simulated by client network conditions).
3) Client SDK issues a retry (default retry policy) that re-sends the request; sometimes original request completes at server while retry is also accepted leading to two downstream invocations.

Observed logs/snippets:
- Edge logs show two requests with different flow IDs but identical payload sizes within ~1s window.
- Downstream function logs show identical tool invocation IDs missing in idempotency store.
- Header dumps show original request had header: "X-Idempotency-Key: sha256:9f8a..."; retry sometimes arrives with altered Content-Type boundary ordering and header length differences.

Initial hypothesis:
- The edge proxy or an intermediate HTTP/2/HTTP/3 translation is rewriting or truncating the idempotency header or canonicalization of multipart boundaries is inconsistent between first and retried request. This causes idempotency hashing in our front-end to compute different keys and accept both requests.
- Binary payload normalization (boundary ordering, canonical whitespace) can alter the server-side hash if SDK does not supply explicit idempotency key.

Immediate customer ask:
- Guidance on SDK settings and a short-term workaround to avoid duplicates while we investigate a permanent fix.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Diego Ramirez: Reproduced locally by forcing a 504 at the edge and allowing SDK retry. Confirmed duplicate downstream invocation in staging-edge using python-sdk 2.1.3.

2026-03-10 11:40 - SRE Team: Captured tcpdump and header logs; observed HTTP/2 HPACK header block fragmentation for large headers when connection migration occurs. The X-Idempotency-Key header is present but sometimes split across frames and our edge-side header reassembly truncates trailing bytes if length > 8192 bytes before normalization step.

2026-03-10 13:05 - SDK Team: Noted python-sdk previously relied on auto-generated SHA256-of-body idempotency when user doesn't provide X-Idempotency-Key. When multipart boundary order changes, computed hash can diverge between original and retry.
Tested deterministic idempotency with explicit short keys — duplicates disappeared in local repro.

2026-03-11 08:30 - Edge Team: Found an edge proxy config that rewrites headers for caching purposes; header size limit and a recent HPACK encoder change in our CDN caused header truncation for some long metadata headers. Preparing a config patch to increase header reassembly buffer and avoid truncation.
2026-03-11 14:22 - Support: Reached out to customer with temporary recommendations and request to try SDK update/workaround.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:02 - Customer (BrightWrite Labs) - Elena Garcia: We've observed duplicates twice today after a larger upload; our downstream team flagged doubled charges for two customers. Happy to test any suggested workaround ASAP.

2026-03-10 10:45 - Support (Maya Thompson): Thanks Elena — we're investigating. Can you confirm SDK version and whether you're setting an explicit X-Idempotency-Key? Also please share a redacted request/response pair if possible.

2026-03-10 11:50 - SRE (Diego Ramirez): We reproduced and are collecting packet captures. Short-term: set a deterministic X-Idempotency-Key on the client (<= 64 bytes) and disable SDK auto-body-hash behavior until we ship an edge fix.
2026-03-11 09:00 - Customer (Elena Garcia): Applied explicit idempotency header per instructions, observed no duplicates in 6h of traffic. Will monitor and report back.
resolution:
Workaround applied and validated by customer: set an explicit, short X-Idempotency-Key (e.g., UUIDv4 or base64url truncated to <=64 chars) on each upload request and upgrade to python-sdk 2.1.4-beta which exposes a helper to produce consistent idempotency keys for multipart uploads.
Permanent fix: Edge Team to deploy header reassembly buffer increase and HPACK encoder revert in next edge canary (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/1582). Rollout plan: canary in us-west staging 2026-03-14, gradual prod rollout 2026-03-15 -> 2026-03-17.
Post-mortem action items:
- INT-900123: Add automated unit test for multipart canonicalization in SDK hash path.
- INT-900124: Add integration test on staging-edge to detect header truncation regressions.
- Update public SDK doc note on idempotency with binary attachments and recommend explicit X-Idempotency-Key for uploads.
Status: Customer validated workaround; permanent edge fix scheduled and linked PR in review.
next_steps: Monitor customer telemetry for duplicate rate for 48h after workaround (owner: Support)
Edge PR merge and canary rollout (owner: Edge Team)
SDK patch release 2.1.4 with helper + docs update (owner: SDK Team)
Close ticket once prod rollout complete and duplicate rate < 0.05% for BrightWrite Labs (criteria)
